title: Contrast linkers
titleVi: Từ nối chỉ sự tương phản
summary: although/though/even though + mệnh đề, despite/in spite of + danh từ, however/whereas — dùng đúng loại từ nối.
whyItMatters: Đây là nhóm từ nối quyết định điểm **Coherence and Cohesion**. Lỗi phổ biến nhất không phải nghĩa mà là **cấu trúc**: *despite of*, *although the rain*, *however the cost rose*. Ở band 7.5, bạn phải chọn đúng loại từ nối cho đúng loại thành phần theo sau, và biết khi nào dùng *whereas* thay cho *but*.

sections.heading: although, though, even though + a clause
body: These three introduce a **full clause** (subject + verb). **Although** is the neutral written form: *Although the scheme was popular, it was cancelled.* **Though** is slightly more informal and can also go at the end of a sentence: *The scheme was popular. It was cancelled, though.*
**Even though** marks a stronger contrast — the fact is surprising or inconvenient: *Even though funding doubled, waiting times did not fall.* Use it when the reader might expect the opposite result.
The clause can come first or second. When it comes first, use a comma: *Although the cost fell, demand remained weak.* No comma is needed when the main clause comes first.

examples.right: Although renewables are cheaper, grid investment remains the bottleneck.
examples.wrong: Although renewables are cheaper, but grid investment remains the bottleneck.

examples.right: The policy was popular. It was cancelled, though.
examples.note: **though** at the end = however, in informal style.

examples.right: Even though the evidence was clear, the ministry delayed the ban.
examples.note: Strong contrast: the delay is surprising.

sections.heading: despite, in spite of + noun or -ing
body: **Despite** and **in spite of** take a **noun, a pronoun or an -ing form** — never a clause. *Despite the cost, the project continued.* *In spite of being warned, they proceeded.*
**Despite** never takes *of*: *despite of the cost* is wrong. **In spite of** always takes *of*. This is the single most common error in this group.
To use a clause, either add **the fact that** (*despite the fact that costs rose*) or switch to **although**. The first is formal and useful in Task 2; the second is simpler and safer.

rows: whereas costs fell in the north

sections.heading: however, nevertheless, even so: sentence adverbs
body: **However, nevertheless, nonetheless, even so** are **sentence adverbs**, not conjunctions. They join two separate sentences and need punctuation: *The cost fell. However, demand did not recover.*

Do not use them as if they were *but*: *However the cost fell, demand did not recover* is wrong because *however* cannot sit inside a clause as a conjunction. Either put a full stop or semicolon before it, and a comma after.
**Even so** is the most conversational of the four; **nevertheless** and **nonetheless** are the most formal. In an essay, one *however* per paragraph is enough — repeated, it becomes a tic.

examples.right: The technology is now affordable. Nevertheless, uptake remains low in rural areas.
examples.wrong: The technology is now affordable, nevertheless uptake remains low in rural areas.
examples.note: A comma splice: use a full stop or a semicolon before **nevertheless**.

examples.right: Funding increased sharply; however, staffing levels barely changed.
examples.note: Semicolon + however + comma is acceptable in formal writing.

examples.right: The scheme was well designed. Even so, it failed to reach the poorest households.
examples.note: **Even so** = in spite of that, referring back to the whole previous sentence.

sections.heading: whereas and while: contrast inside one sentence
body: **Whereas** and **while** join two clauses in a single sentence and set them against each other: *Urban incomes rose by 12%, whereas rural incomes stagnated.*
**Whereas** is the more formal and more explicitly contrastive choice; **while** can also mean *at the same time*, so in careful academic writing *whereas* removes the ambiguity.
This is the structure examiners associate with band 8 comparison: two parallel clauses, one shared verb of change, and a clear contrast.

examples.right: Graduates in engineering earned above the median, whereas arts graduates earned well below it.
While the north gained manufacturing jobs, the south lost them.
Whereas the first chart shows total spending, the second shows spending per household.
examples.wrong: Whereas the first chart shows total spending, however the second shows spending per household.

sections.heading: even, as and as if: contrast and comparison
body: **Even** emphasises an extreme case within a contrast: *Even the wealthiest districts struggled to recruit teachers.* Put it immediately before the element it highlights.

**As** introduces a **clause** (*As the report notes, …*) or a role (*She works as a nurse*). **Like** introduces a **noun** (*Cities like Da Nang*). In formal writing, do not use *like* before a clause: *like I said* is conversational.

**As if / as though** introduce an imagined situation. For something untrue, use a past tense: *The city is spending as if the boom would last forever* — the boom is not certain to last. This is the same distancing you use in second conditionals.

examples.right: Even the most experienced teachers found the syllabus demanding.
As the chart shows, demand peaked in 2012.
The economy is growing as if the recession had never happened.
examples.wrong: The economy is growing like the recession had never happened.
examples.note: Before a clause, use **as if**, not *like*.

commonMistakes.wrong: Despite of the high cost, the project continued.
commonMistakes.right: Despite the high cost, the project continued.
commonMistakes.why: **despite** không đi với *of*. Chỉ **in spite of** mới có *of*.

commonMistakes.wrong: Although the high cost, the project continued.
commonMistakes.right: Although the cost was high, the project continued.
commonMistakes.why: **although** cần một **mệnh đề** (chủ ngữ + động từ). Với cụm danh từ, dùng **despite / in spite of**.

commonMistakes.wrong: The cost fell, however demand did not recover.
commonMistakes.right: The cost fell. However, demand did not recover.
commonMistakes.why: **however** là trạng từ nối câu, không phải liên từ. Cần dấu chấm hoặc chấm phẩy trước nó, và dấu phẩy sau.

commonMistakes.wrong: Even although funding doubled, waiting times did not fall.
commonMistakes.right: Even though funding doubled, waiting times did not fall.
commonMistakes.why: Cụm đúng là **even though**, không phải *even although*.

commonMistakes.wrong: The city is spending like the boom would last forever.
commonMistakes.right: The city is spending as if the boom would last forever.
commonMistakes.why: Trước một **mệnh đề**, dùng **as if / as though**. *Like* chỉ đứng trước danh từ hoặc đại từ.

ieltsTips: Dùng **whereas** để so sánh hai nhóm trong cùng một câu Task 1: *Households in the capital spent 30% of income on rent, **whereas** those in rural areas spent under 15%.* Câu song song, rõ ràng, đúng chuẩn học thuật.
Dùng **despite + -ing** để nén mệnh đề và tăng mật độ thông tin: ***Despite receiving** substantial funding, the programme failed to improve literacy.* Gọn hơn *Although it received…*

Đặt **Even though** ở đầu câu để mở đoạn thân bài phản biện: ***Even though** the policy was popular, its costs fell disproportionately on low-income households.* Câu này tạo lập trường phê bình ngay lập tức.
Đừng dùng quá hai từ nối tương phản trong một đoạn. Nếu đã có *although* và *however*, câu tiếp theo nên dùng **whereas**, hoặc bỏ từ nối và để quan hệ tự thể hiện.

exercises.explanation: A noun phrase follows → **Despite**; *Despite of* is wrong.

exercises.explanation: Two parallel clauses inside one sentence → **whereas**.

exercises.explanation: Before a clause with an unreal situation → **as if**.

exercises.explanation: An -ing form follows → **Despite / In spite of**.

___ the most experienced teachers found the syllabus demanding.
exercises.explanation: **Even** before the noun phrase highlights an extreme case.

exercises.explanation: **however** after a semicolon, followed by a comma.
